title: Interchange a finite open covering and local proper surjections
statement: Let $S$ be a reduced Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $S=\bigcup_{i=1}^r U_i$ be a finite Zariski open cover [def-weil-open-immersion]. For each $i$, let $z_i:Z_i\to U_i$ be proper and surjective [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], and assume that the composite $Z_i\to S$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology]. Then there exist an object $Y\to S$ of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, proper and surjective, and, for every $i$, a $U_i$-morphism $Y\times_SU_i\to Z_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular the inverse images of the $U_i$ are a finite open cover of $Y$ whose maps to $S$ factor through the $Z_i$. The schemes $S$ and $Y$ may have several irreducible components; no integrality or quasi-excellence hypothesis is imposed. If $S$ is empty, $r=0$ and $Y=\varnothing$ are allowed.

source.place: Expose II Theorem 3.2.1, proof for parameter 1, printed p.29: compactify the local proper surjections, take their product and its dominant reduced part (II 1.2.5 and Proposition 1.2.8). For a reducible base, add the reduced closed complement S minus U_i to each compactification before taking the product; this retains surjectivity without assuming every U_i dense.

proof.text: For each $i$ apply [lem-per-open-proper-dense-compactification] to $Z_i\to U_i\hookrightarrow S$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given properness and membership of $Z_i\to S$ in $\operatorname{alt}/S$. Obtain a proper $b_i:B_i\to S$ with $B_i\times_SU_i\simeq Z_i$. For every component-generic point $s$ of $S$, $(B_i)_s$ is finite over $\kappa(s)$, and is empty if $s\notin U_i$.

source.place: II 3.2.1, ordinary-case proof, p.29: compactification and its restriction to the original open.

proof.text: Let $C_i$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme of $S$ on $S\setminus U_i$, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Form $W_i=B_i\amalg C_i$ over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; it is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-coproduct]. Its image contains $U_i$, because $B_i|_{U_i}\simeq Z_i\to U_i$ is surjective, and contains $S\setminus U_i$ through $C_i$. Thus $W_i\to S$ is surjective. The closed complement has empty inverse image over $U_i$, so $W_i|_{U_i}\simeq Z_i$. Adding this summand is necessary when $U_i$ misses an irreducible component of $S$.

source.place: II 3.2.1 ordinary proof, p.29, compactifications; extension to a reducible base by adjoining the reduced closed complement.

proof.text: For every component-generic $s$, the fibre $(C_i)_s$ is a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, by the closed-immersion base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], hence either that field spectrum or empty: on this affine the defining ideal has quotient $\kappa(s)/I$ with $I=0$ or $I=\kappa(s)$. Base change of the coproduct identifies $(W_i)_s$ with $(B_i)_s\amalg(C_i)_s$ [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct]. The first summand is affine with finite-dimensional coordinate algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] the coproduct has coordinate algebra the product of that algebra and $\kappa(s)$ or the zero ring. This is finite-dimensional, so $(W_i)_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is finite by the affine definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: II 1.2.6, p.25, finite generic fibres of the product; closed-complement summands are computed over a field.

proof.text: Set $P_0=S$ and $P_k=P_{k-1}\times_SW_k$ for $1\leq k\leq r$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Inductively $P_k\to P_{k-1}$ is the base change of the proper surjection $W_k\to S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] it is proper and surjective. Composition preserves properness, and composition of surjective functions is surjective. Starting with the identity $P_0\to S$, this proves $P=P_r\to S$ proper and surjective. At every generic $s$, $(P_k)_s\simeq(P_{k-1})_s\times_{\kappa(s)}(W_k)_s$ by the universal property. Starting with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] prove inductively that every $(P_k)_s$ is finite. These assertions include $r=0$.

source.place: II 3.2.1 ordinary proof, p.29, product of compactifications; II 1.2.6 for finite generic fibre.

proof.text: Let $Y=P_{\mathrm{md}}$ be the dominant reduced part of [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection]. The base $S$ is reduced, so $S_{\mathrm{md}}=S$; the proper-surjection clause applied to $P\to S$ gives a proper surjection $Y\to S$. The same statement makes $Y$ reduced, finite type over $S$, and maximally dominant, and identifies $Y_s$ with $((P)_s)_{\mathrm{red}}$. To check the remaining finite residue-field condition, write the finite generic fibre $P_s=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ finite-dimensional over $K=\kappa(s)$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim]. Every prime quotient of $A$ is a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]. Thus all primes are maximal; by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] there are no strict chains of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, so the fibre has dimension zero, and its reduced closed subscheme $Y_s$ also has dimension zero. It is finite type over $K$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] makes it finite discrete. Each point is isolated; [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-residue-finite] applied to $Y\to S$ now proves the finite residue-field condition at every generic point of $Y$. Consequently $Y\to S$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ by [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology].

source.place: II 1.2.5 and Proposition 1.2.8, pp.25--26, applied as in II 3.2.1, p.29.

proof.text: Compose $Y\hookrightarrow P$ with the $i$th product projection $P\to W_i$. After base change to $U_i$, [def-pc-fibre-product] gives a $U_i$-morphism $Y\times_SU_i\to W_i\times_SU_i\simeq Z_i$; the last identification is the one constructed in step 2, since the complement summand restricts to the empty scheme [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct]. Put $V_i=Y\times_SU_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] these are the inverse-image open subschemes, and they cover $Y$: for any $y\in Y$, its image in $S$ belongs to some $U_i$, whence $y\in V_i$. All the maps have been constructed over $S$, so their composites $V_i\to S$ factor through $Z_i\to S$. If $S$ is empty then all these schemes are empty, and with $r=0$ the construction gives $P_0=S$ and $Y=\varnothing$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q103-67a83f5e1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read ILO Exposé II: Theorem 3.2.1 and its ℓ=1 proof (p.29), 1.1.7 and 1.2.2 (p.24), and 1.2.5, 1.2.6 and 1.2.8 (pp.25-26), plus Stacks 0F41 (flat.tex theorem-nagata). The item's statement is the same as on the base and matches how lem-per-ordinary-alteration-proper-refinement uses it in step 4. The six steps follow ILO's construction: compactify each local map, form the product, take the dominant part. The one addition is the reduced complement S∖U_i joined to each compactification in step 2. This is correct and needed on a reducible base: with S = Spec k ⊔ Spec k′ and U = Spec k, the compactification alone does not cover S. Every cited statement says what its step takes from it: the coproduct base-change lemma, closed-immersion and proper-coproduct properness, base change of closed immersions and proper maps, surjective base change, finite permanence and composition, finite-over-field affine, finite-dimensional domain is a field, dimension-0 finite type is discrete, and isolated fibre point has finite residue field. Step 5 uses dominant-part-coreflection exactly as stated: general Noetherian base, S_md = S because S is reduced, the proper-surjection clause, and Y_s = (P_s)_red. The new node lem-per-open-proper-dense-compactification is true. I checked it myself: Nagata gives a dense compactification; Z → B_U is open, proper and dense, hence an isomorphism; B_s is empty off U because every generic point of B lies in Z; and Z_s is finite by 1.1.7. The empty cases also hold. It has a statement only, with three kinds of search recorded. It is not a duplicate of det-nagata-theorem-dense, lem-sfb-over-compactification-composite-cartesian (which has no generic-fibre clauses) or lem-per-finite-generic-dominant-parts (integral base), and it does not restate the item. Batch-5 check: def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology reaching def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary is a general definition, not part of the trace-formula or duality proofs, and the item's statement already cited it on the base, so it is acceptable. Artin-Gabber check: lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve no longer reaches the item, the coreflection node or qe-weak-uniformization-cover (BFS: unreached). The item is reached through the sk-thm-sf-package / sfb Gabber-alteration chain, so the 2026-10-19 restriction on artin-gabber and its three children does not apply. dominant-part-coreflection is a reviewed generic ILO 1.2.5/1.2.8 lemma, justified at step 5. I accept all 19 generic scheme tool_uses. No SGA source is cited. No changes.
